messages:
alex_support: FYI customer on Private had a major outage after a peering change this morning — app-to-private-api failing with TLS handshake errors and DNS timeouts. They reported: 
- app logs: "tls: handshake failure (certificate verify)"
- curl to private-api.redwood.internal -> NXDOMAIN occasionally, sometimes long latency
- IKE logs show SA up then immediately rekey, traffic not flowing

mira_netops: :eyes: any change to egress allowlists / firewall rules on their side or ours?

alex_support: Customer said they pushed a BGP filter on their DX side to only allow specific prefixes and added a strict egress allowlist earlier today (per ticket). They also rotated a static secret for the IPsec peer.

raj_engineer: Possible lead: if OCSP/CRL OCSP stapling queries are blocked by egress ACLs, many TLS stacks will fail cert verification; also NAT-T/ESP fragmentation and MTU clamping can cause intermittent AES-GCM TLS failures. Need packet captures and IPsec debug.

mira_netops: Agreed. Ask customer for: 
1) `show ipsec sa` / `sudo ipsec statusall` output
2) `show bgp summary` on their edge and our side
3) tcpdump of UDP 500/4500 and proto 50 (ESP) from their GW during repro
4) any fw/acl entries they added (full rules, not just summary)

alex_support: Sent repro steps and requested captures. Customer attached `journalctl` showing repeated IKE rekeys every ~10s and an nginx error: `TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate`

raj_engineer: Quick debug checklist (to send to customer):
````
- Verify egress allowlist permits outbound TCP/443 to OCSP responders and TCP/80 if needed for CRL
- Allow outbound UDP 500/4500 and IP protocol 50 (ESP) between peers
- Check MTU: set ipsec tunnel MTU clamp to 1400 on their firewall if using path MTU issues
- Confirm IKE/IKEv2 proposals match (encryption/hash/lifetime) on both sides
- If behind NAT, ensure NAT-T (UDP encapsulation) not being blocked by stateful device
````

mira_netops: Add also to check DNS: if their resolver hits upstream over the peering, BGP route suppression or missing host routes could cause NXDOMAINs. Ask for `dig +trace private-api.redwood.internal` from their app host and from the edge.

alex_support: Customer returned a tcpdump snippet: shows SYN to our private API IP, then RST, and several outgoing connections to ocsp.globalsign.com failing with ICMP administratively prohibited. They also forwarded their firewall rule that denies outbound to any internet host unless explicitly allowed.

raj_engineer: That matches OCSP being blocked. When certificates are stapled the server may still validate OCSP on first handshake depending on client. Recommend they allow outbound to known OCSP responders for the CA used by our cert (include list). Immediate mitigation: add explicit egress allowlist entries for OCSP responder IPs and for our control-plane endpoints, and allow UDP 500/4500 + ESP between peers.

mira_netops: For longer term: we should provide them a minimal egress CIDR set and CA OCSP FQDNs to allow. Also suggest implementing health-check fallback: allow the Private control-plane to be reachable via an alternate route (our Dedicated fallback) during peering changes.

alex_support: I'll propose temporary workaround and coordinate change window. Customer asked if we can temporarily disable OCSP checks on our side — not ideal. Any objection?

raj_engineer: We should not disable OCSP. We can (a) provide a list of OCSP responder IPs/FQDNs + control-plane endpoints to allow, (b) open a narrow support window to validate with captures. If they can't change fw quickly, ask them to route control-plane traffic over their management VPN or allowlist our control-plane CIDRs.

mira_netops: Also ask them to confirm BGP advertisements: we saw BGP withdraws from their DX during the same time window in our monitoring. If routes were suppressed, app hosts may have tried DNS queries to the wrong resolver.

alex_support: Noted. I've scheduled a 30m call with customer and raj for packet review in 20m. Sending them the command snippets: 
```
sudo tcpdump -n -i any 'port 500 or port 4500 or icmp or proto 50' -w /tmp/ipsec-trace.pcap
sudo tcpdump -n -i any 'tcp port 80 or tcp port 443 and host ocsp.globalsign.com' -w /tmp/ocsp-trace.pcap
sudo ipsec statusall > /tmp/ipsec-status.txt
show bgp neighbors > /tmp/bgp-neigh.txt
```

slo-bot: Incident SLA window set: Sev-2 support 2h response target.

raj_engineer: I'll be on the call and will review pcap live. If we confirm ocsp/egress block + BGP withdraws, run change: add egress allow entries for OCSP + control-plane CIDRs and allow UDP 500/4500 + ESP (protocol 50). Also consider MTU clamp 1400 on their edge for immediate relief.

alex_support: Thanks team. I'll update thread after call. :thumbsup:
